blocks.caption: Chapter 2 key terms
rows: Computational thinking
Understanding a problem, breaking it into smaller parts and solving it step by step with logical thinking
Decomposition
Breaking a large or complex problem into smaller, manageable parts
Algorithm
A step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem or perform a task
Logic
A formal way of representing facts, statements and rules for correct reasoning and decisions
Proposition
A statement that is either true or false, but not both
Compound proposition
Two or more simple propositions joined by AND, OR or NOT
Truth table
A table of an expression's truth values for every combination of inputs
Propositional equivalence
Two expressions having the same truth values in all cases
Propositional satisfiability
A proposition is satisfiable if it is true in at least one case
Predicate logic
Logic that represents statements using subjects, properties, variables and relationships
Predicate
An expression describing a property or relationship of a subject
Quantifier
Shows how many objects a statement applies to: for all, or there exists
Logical inference
Drawing a correct conclusion from given facts
Deduction
Deriving a specific conclusion from general rules or known facts
